title: The Walk: one sentence per stop

segments.text: A complex number is a move: turn, then stretch.
Same dot, two addresses.
Multiplying is a move; adding is a slide.
A circle is every point one stretch away from the centre.
arg z is every name; Arg z is the home step; z never moves.
Any name works for a power; report the home step.
Roots need every name; k = n is k = 0 again.
A curve is a point that moves; time is the clock the w-plane will keep.
Open, closed, boundary: all sentences about a tiny disk.
Functions built from moves keep circles and rays.
One move and one slide, for the whole plane.
Push the line forward with y as the clock, then eliminate y.
Principal means the home step only.
A branch is a continuous choice of name; cut where the question does not look.
Invert the length, mirror the angle; zero goes to infinity, so the circle opens.
Every direction must agree.
Differentiable means one move up close; the derivative is that move.
Cauchy-Riemann says no mirror.
Draw it, push it forward, read it.
Every picture is a shadow of one object.
Same place, new numbers.
Which place, which address, which names.
